tex_content.html:
Proposition
[Odd map of Sn has odd degree] ↗ cor:homology-spheres 1. ch2:2B.6\group Cellular Homology

If $f:S^n\to S^n$ satisfies $f(-x)=-f(x)$, then $\deg f$ is odd.
Proof

\sketch Use the transfer exact sequence for $S^n\to \mathbb {RP}^n$ with $\mathbb {Z}_2$ coefficients. An odd map induces a morphism of transfer sequences; induction and exactness show that $f_*$ on top homology is an isomorphism. The degree map with these coefficients is multiplication by $\deg f\bmod 2$.

□
